questions.explain: A model that writes great summaries can still be dangerous at choosing actions, so each task type needs its own metric and minimum bar.
options: Because different DBA tasks (classification, ranking, generation, detection) need different metrics and minimum bars
Because per-task evaluation uses fewer tokens than a single overall score
Because SQL Server only supports one evaluation metric at a time
Because public leaderboards require per-task submissions
questions.q: Why does the chapter recommend evaluating AI models per task rather than scoring a model once overall?

questions.explain: A human-forced plan confirmed as the fix gives you ground truth — the regressed query text plus the known-good plan_id.
options: It provides a labeled example: the regressed query plus the plan_id a human verified as the fix
It proves the model can write T-SQL without hallucinating
It measures token cost per resolved incident
It tests whether the model can detect prompt injection
questions.q: What makes a Query Store plan regression with a forced plan a good golden-dataset case?

questions.explain: Safety is non-negotiable: any output containing unauthorized destructive statements like DROP TABLE fails outright, regardless of task correctness.
options: Because the harness can only run one scorer per case
To reduce token usage by skipping expensive scorers
Because a correct answer wrapped around an unauthorized destructive statement must still fail the case
Because JSON parsing requires the safety check first
questions.q: In the offline eval harness, why does the safety gate run BEFORE the task scorer on every case?

questions.explain: A model grading its own output exhibits self-preference bias; judge-model separation plus calibration against human graders keeps scoring honest.
options: Stronger models cost fewer tokens per evaluation
To avoid self-preference bias, where a model favors its own style when grading itself
Because the generator cannot output JSON
Because judges must run at temperature 1.0
questions.q: Why should the LLM-as-judge be a different, stronger model than the generator?

questions.explain: Healthy triage models abstain on 5-15% of ambiguous cases; zero abstention means the model guesses instead of escalating.
options: Perfect confidence and readiness for full autonomy
A red flag — a model that never says 'insufficient data' is lying some of the time
That the golden dataset is too small
That token cost per incident is minimized
questions.q: What does a 0% abstention rate indicate about a DBA triage model?

title: Evaluating AI Models for Database Tasks
